Rules:
- Each assignment names a role and either a user or a group; if it names a group, every member of the group holds the role. Groups may list other groups as members. A user belongs to a group if the group lists the user or lists a group the user belongs to, over any number of steps. Belonging never runs downward: the users listed in an outer group do not belong to the groups listed inside it.
- Assignments reach downward only: the namespace where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; namespaces beside it or above it are not.
- Exception for sealed namespaces: an assignment never passes into a sealed namespace from a namespace above it, so the sealed namespace and everything below it stay out of its reach. A seal does nothing to an assignment made at the sealed namespace or below it, and nothing to namespaces that are not inside the sealed namespace.
- A role allows the actions listed for it. A role that extends another role also allows everything the other role allows, including what that role gets from a role it extends. Extension works one way only: the extended role gains nothing.
- Actions can include other actions, exactly as listed. Being allowed an action means being allowed every action it includes, directly or through a chain of listed inclusions. An inclusion is never read backwards, and actions without a listed link do not include each other.
- A deny entry names a user or a group, one action and one namespace. It applies to a request when the requester is that user or a member of that group (nested membership counts), the requested action is exactly the named action, and the requested namespace is the named namespace or lies below it; a seal does not stop a deny entry. A deny entry that applies beats every assignment. It affects no other action: denying X does not block Y, even if X includes Y or Y includes X.
- A request is allowed if at least one assignment gives the requester a role that allows the requested action and covers the requested namespace, and no deny entry applies. Otherwise it is not allowed.
